questions.q: What is the real limit of Lesson 6's manual SELECT COUNT(*) parity check?
options: It only works the first time it's run and can never be repeated
It only proved the warehouse was correct once, on the day it was written — but the warehouse refreshes nightly, unattended
It cannot be run in SQL Server Management Studio
It only checks dw.DimProduct, not the fact table
questions.explain: A one-time manual check can't protect a warehouse that refreshes every night with no human re-running it by hand.

questions.q: In the night-40 scenario, what actually happens if a batch of orders with an unresolved TerritoryID loads and nobody catches it?
options: The warehouse refresh fails loudly and sends an alert automatically
All three front-ends — Power BI, Tableau, and Excel — quietly under-report the same missing orders the next morning, with nobody noticing
Only the Power BI dashboard is affected, since Tableau and Excel use different data
The orders are automatically deleted from the source system
questions.explain: Because all three front-ends read the same warehouse, a silent data-quality problem in the warehouse affects all three deliverables identically, with no error raised to flag it.

questions.q: Which pandas technique is used to catch duplicate rows that got loaded into the warehouse more than once?
options: .isna().sum()
.duplicated()
len(df) comparisons
A set difference between two key columns
questions.explain: .duplicated() flags rows that repeat, which is the real pandas technique for catching rows loaded more than once.

questions.q: Why can't this data-quality validation simply live inside the Power BI data model?
options: Power BI doesn't support any kind of data validation at all
Power BI, Tableau, and Excel are all read-only consumers by design; a check inside only one of them would never catch a problem before the other two also displayed it
Because pandas cannot connect to Power BI
Because Power BI data models are deleted after each refresh
questions.explain: The validation has to sit between the warehouse and all three consumers, independent of any single tool, so it catches a problem before any front-end displays it.

questions.q: What pandas technique catches an orphaned foreign key — a fact row's key that doesn't actually exist in its dimension?
options: A set difference between the fact table's key column and the dimension's key column
.duplicated() on the fact table alone
Sorting the dimension table alphabetically
Counting the number of columns in each table
questions.explain: Taking the set of keys used in the fact table and subtracting the set of keys that actually exist in the dimension surfaces exactly the orphaned values, if any exist.
